newsitem.title: USA: Sano in new trials on anti-smoking product.
newsitem.headline: Sano in new trials on anti-smoking product.

text.p: Sano Corp said Monday it has began a Phase III human trial program on its proprietary drug-in-adhesive patch product designed to make users stop smoking.

Called the Nicotine/Mecamylamine Transdermal System, trials for the product are being conducted at eight U.S. centers, will encompass over 1,000 smokers, and will be conducted for about six months, the company said.

"By blocking the nicotinic receptors that produce the rewarding effects of nicotine, this therapy can potentially diminish satisfaction from smoking, reduce craving, and thus reinforce abstinence," said Scott Leischow, an assistant professor of health education at the University of Arizona College of Medicine who is a primary investigator in the studies.

"We are enthusiastic about these studies because we believe the nicotine/mecamylamine patch is the first pharmaceutical approach that addresses a fundamental issue in smoking, namely the feeling of satisfaction," he said.

The Nicotine/Mecamylamine Transdermal System is comprised of Sano's drug-in-adhesive patch through which its patented nicotine and mecamylamine combination are simultaneously delivered directly through the patient's skin, the company said.

The pharmacological action of the combination therapy is intended to increase smokers' continuous abstinence by reducing the satisfaction that smokers experience from cigarettes, and reducing their craving, without the need for counseling, it said.

To create a viable commercial product, Sano said it developed a single patch which delivers both the nicotine and mecamylamine at the appropriate doses. In 1996, Sano said it completed a 260-patient Phase II study with its combination nicotine/mecamylamine patch which identified the therapeutic dose range.
